LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 12.3.1 QUESTION TAGS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.3: Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is a question tag?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify question tags from a print or digital text for information
2. form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals
3. use question tags correctly in oral and written texts
4. appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 12.3.1 QUESTION TAGS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 12.3.1 QUESTION TAGS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify question tags from a print or digital text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify question tags from a print or digital text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify question tags from a print or digital text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify question tags from a print or digital text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals

What this means
In this part you learn to form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use question tags correctly in oral and written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to use question tags correctly in oral and written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use question tags correctly in oral and written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use question tags correctly in oral and written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify question tags from a print or digital text for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags to a partner. (skill: form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: use question tags correctly in oral and written texts)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the importance of well- formed sentences in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify question tags from a print or digital text for information.
3. Practise this skill: form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals.
4. Practise this skill: use question tags correctly in oral and written texts.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is a question tag?
2. How do we form question tags?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Question Tags means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify question tags from a print or digital text for information.
5. Be able to: form question tags from verbs to be, verbs to have, verbs to do and modals.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
